title: Integral constructible internal Hom
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi=\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\geq1$ and $\widehat R_X=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_X$ on the small pro-etale site of $X$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Work in the ambient derived category of $\widehat R_X$-modules, with the full subcategory $D^b_c(X,R)$ of derived-complete complexes whose finite reductions are bounded constructible and have cohomological supports in one interval independent of $n$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. For an ambient complex $M$ write $M_n=M\otimes^L_{\widehat R_X}(A_n)_X$ for its reduction in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction].

For every $K,L\in D^b_c(X,R)$, their ambient derived internal Hom $H=R\mathcal Hom_{\widehat R_X}(K,L)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] belongs to $D^b_c(X,R)$. For every $n\geq1$ the canonical evaluation-defined comparison is an isomorphism in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$,
$$
 H_n\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{(A_n)_X}(K_n,L_n).
$$
More precisely, let $a\leq b$ and $c\leq e$ be integers and $d\geq0$ an integer with $\dim X\leq d$, where dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. If every $K_n$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ over $(A_n)_X$ and every $L_n$ has Tor amplitude in $[c,e]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude], then every $H_n$ has Tor amplitude in $[c-b-2d,e-a+2d]$, uniformly in $n$.

proof.text: Put $H=R\mathcal Hom_{\widehat R_X}(K,L)$. The integral-category definition makes $L$ derived complete. Apply [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction]: $H$ is derived complete, and for each $n\geq1$ the evaluation-defined comparison $H_n\xrightarrow{\sim}T_n=R\mathcal Hom_{(A_n)_X}(K_n,L_n)$ is an isomorphism in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$.

By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], $\dim X<\infty$; its chain-supremum definition gives an integer $d_0\geq0$ bounding it (take $d_0=0$ if $X=\emptyset$). The integral-category definition makes $K_1,L_1$ bounded constructible. Choose support intervals $[\alpha,\beta]$, $[\gamma,\epsilon]$, choosing any nonempty interval for a zero input. Apply [lem-coef-residue-controlled-finite-homs] with $d_0$. Every $T_n$ is bounded constructible and has cohomology supported in the same interval $[\gamma-\beta-2d_0,\epsilon-\alpha+2d_0]$. Through step 1, all $H_n$ have these properties. Together with completeness from step 1 these are precisely the defining conditions for $H\in D^b_c(X,R)$.

source.place: Sentences 2–4: the extracted finite-level estimate and integral membership

proof.text: For the quantitative clause use the supplied $a,b,c,e,d$. For $n=1$ test the assumed Tor bounds of $K_1,L_1$ against $(A_1)_X$ in degree zero. The tensor-unit identification follows on a K-flat representative $P$ from the inverse chain maps $P\otimes(A_1)_X\to P$, $x\otimes r\mapsto rx$, and $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Thus their residue cohomology is supported in $[a,b]$ and $[c,e]$. Apply [lem-coef-residue-controlled-finite-homs] with these intervals and $d$ to get Tor amplitude $[c-b-2d,e-a+2d]$ for every $T_n$. The isomorphism in step 1 gives the same bound for $H_n$: for any degree-zero $(A_n)_X$-module $M$, tensoring that isomorphism with $M$ identifies the tested cohomology. Bounded constructibility and support in step 2 likewise pass along an isomorphism by applying cohomology. All tests remain over $(A_n)_X$.

source.place: Sentence 3, quantitative interval, and final sentence, tensor-unit test

split_report.summary: Human-requested re-split: extracted the residue-controlled uniform finite-level internal-Hom estimate, including the output cohomology bound, into one independent statement-only node. The item retains the original statement, ambient completeness and canonical comparison, dimension choice, integral-membership assembly, and the arbitrary supplied-interval clause. No argument of the old proof is discarded.
split_report.blueprint: The new node carries sentences 2–3 of the blueprint proof and the tensor-unit cohomology deduction needed by its final sentence (old steps 1 and 4 plus the unit test in old step 5). Parent step 1 carries sentence 1; step 2 retains the dimension choice and final membership assembly; step 3 retains the supplied-interval clause with an explicit residue tensor-unit test.

tool_uses.why: Generic dimension finiteness for a finite-type scheme over a field, needed to choose one bound before proving integral constructibility; the biduality unit has no statement providing this geometric bound.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q64-301cdfdf2 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Answers the 2026-10-21 human re-split note (old proof 3181 characters, at least 1 new node required). The item's statement, stmt_deps, source and tool_uses are byte-identical to live; only the proof fields changed. The new proof is 3 steps, about 1844 characters. Each old step has a carrier. Old step 2 (lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction: canonical evaluation-transpose iso and completeness) is parent step 1. Old step 3 (dimension bound d_0, including X empty) is parent step 2. Old steps 1, 4 and the unit test of 5 (residue-Tor gives a uniform input Tor interval; cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom at each n; the M=(A_n)_X test gives the cohomological interval) became the statement of the new unsplit node lem-coef-residue-controlled-finite-homs. The definitional assembly of old step 5 is in parent step 2, and the supplied-interval clause is parent step 3, which proves K_1's residue support by an explicit K-flat unit test at n=1. The new node is self-contained, and every notion cites a node that defines it. It has 7 recorded searches across grep, leansearch, loogle and leanfinder, and its source is the main-20261015 proof sentences 2-3 (the same text as master order 2147). Its hypotheses suffice: X over F̄_q with ℓ≠p for residue-tor; separated of finite type, pro-étale site and dim≤d for the finite Hom result. I tested it on a point with K=L=R (interval [0,0]), on K=R/ϖ, L=R (T_n has κ in degrees 0 and 1, matching [0,1]) and on zero inputs. It is not a restatement of the item (no ambient H, no completeness or comparison). A whole-DAG search found no duplicate: the finite-Hom nodes are single-level with finite-Tor inputs, and residue-tor covers one input with no Hom. There is no cycle and no new batch-5 node. The base tool_use lem-kun-dimension-finite-type is kept and accepted. No SGA.
